Fat
FAT
n. and adj. (rendering Hebrew chēleb and shāmēn)
From Old English faett. The Hebrew chēleb denotes the hard suet about the kidneys and inwards of a sacrificial animal, and it was regarded as the richest part — which is why the law reserves it wholly to God and forbids Israel to eat it. From the sacrificial sense the word extends to mean the best of anything: the fat of the land is its choicest produce, and to be fat is to be prosperous.

Biblical Definition

Fat in Scripture is the choicest portion, and the law puts it beyond human use with a formula of striking simplicity: “And the priest shall burn them upon the altar: it is the food of the offering made by fire for a sweet savour: all the fat is the LORD'S” (Lev 3:16). The best is reserved to God, not as something He needs but as a daily lesson in what worship costs. From that the word becomes a figure for abundance, and also for the peculiar spiritual danger abundance brings. The song of Moses uses it to describe a nation ruined by its own prosperity, in a line whose bluntness has never been improved on: “But Jeshurun waxed fat, and kicked: thou art waxen fat, thou art grown thick, thou art covered with fatness; then he forsook God which made him, and lightly esteemed the Rock of his salvation” (Deu 32:15). Prosperity did what persecution could not. The prophets then use the word against the very offerings it belonged to, when the offerings are brought by unrepentant men: “I am full of the burnt offerings of rams, and the fat of fed beasts; and I delight not in the blood of bullocks” (Isa 1:11). And Samuel states the ranking that governs the whole sacrificial system, in the sentence that broke Saul: “Hath the LORD as great delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices, as in obeying the voice of the LORD? Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice, and to hearken than the fat of rams” (1Sa 15:22). The fat was God's by law; obedience was God's by right, and the man who offered the one while withholding the other had given Him nothing.

Webster 1828 Definition

The oily concrete substance of animal bodies; in the Levitical law the suet of the sacrifice, reserved wholly to the LORD and forbidden as food; and by extension the best or choicest part — whence the fat of the land, and the fatness that made Jeshurun kick.

expand to see more

FAT, n. 1. A solid oily concrete substance, found in the cellular membrane of animal bodies.

2. The best or richest part of a thing; as the fat of the land. Gen. 45.

3. adj. Fleshy; plump; corpulent; abounding with fat.

4. Rich; wealthy; affluent; as, a fat benefice. Also, fertile; as fat land.

5. In the Levitical law, the suet of the inwards, wholly consumed on the altar; all the fat is the LORD's. Levit. 3. Ye shall eat no manner of fat. Levit. 7.

Key Scripture

Leviticus 3:16 — "And the priest shall burn them upon the altar: it is the food of the offering made by fire for a sweet savour: all the fat is the LORD'S."

Deuteronomy 32:15 — "But Jeshurun waxed fat, and kicked: thou art waxen fat, thou art grown thick, thou art covered with fatness; then he forsook God which made him, and lightly esteemed the Rock of his salvation."

Isaiah 1:11 — "To what purpose is the multitude of your sacrifices unto me? saith the LORD: I am full of the burnt offerings of rams, and the fat of fed beasts; and I delight not in the blood of bullocks, or of lambs, or of he goats."

1 Samuel 15:22 — "And Samuel said, Hath the LORD as great delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices, as in obeying the voice of the LORD? Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice, and to hearken than the fat of rams."

Modern Corruption

Prosperity is treated as an unambiguous sign of God's approval rather than as one of the most dangerous conditions a soul can be in, so that the warning of Jeshurun waxing fat is never applied to the comfortable.

expand to see more

Deu 32:15 describes a sequence that Scripture treats as ordinary rather than exceptional: God prospers a people, the people grow thick with prosperity, and then they forsake the God who prospered them. Jeshurun — the affectionate name for upright Israel — kicked. Agur asks to be given neither poverty nor riches for exactly this reason: lest I be full, and deny thee, and say, Who is the LORD? Where prosperity is read simply as approval, this entire strand of biblical warning becomes unusable, and the comfortable are deprived of the one diagnosis most likely to fit them. The Laodicean church said I am rich, and increased with goods, and have need of nothing, and did not know it was wretched and poor and blind and naked; the danger of fatness is precisely that it is invisible from inside.

The second corruption concerns worship, and 1Sa 15:22 is its cure. Saul had kept back the best of the spoil, intending to sacrifice it, and the reply he received sets the whole sacrificial system in its place: to obey is better than sacrifice, and to hearken than the fat of rams. Religious generosity offered in place of obedience is not a partial payment but a substitution God refuses, and it remains one of the commonest evasions in devout circles — giving abundantly, serving visibly, and withholding the one thing commanded. The principle to recover is the law's own: all the fat is the LORD'S (Lev 3:16). The best belongs to Him by right, and a man who brings Him the fat while keeping back his obedience has inverted the order and given God the cheaper thing.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew chēleb is the suet or fat of a sacrifice, reserved to the LORD and forbidden as food; shāmēn means fat, rich, or fertile; mishmān is fatness or richness of soil.

expand to see more

Hebrew chēleb (H2459) — the fat or suet about the kidneys and inwards; all the fat is the LORD'S (Lev 3:16), and Israel was forbidden to eat it.

Hebrew shāmēn (H8082) — fat, rich, fertile; used of good land, of well-fed beasts, and of prosperous men.

Hebrew Y'shurūn (H3484) — the upright one, a poetic name for Israel; Jeshurun waxed fat, and kicked (Deu 32:15).

Hebrew chēleb hā'ārets — the fat of the land, its choicest produce; promised to Jacob's household in Egypt (Gen 45:18).

Hebrew shāma' (H8085) — to hear and so to obey; to hearken is better than the fat of rams (1Sa 15:22).

Usage

"Of the portion reserved to God: all the fat is the LORD'S (Lev 3:16)."

"Of prosperity as a spiritual danger: Jeshurun waxed fat, and kicked... then he forsook God which made him (Deu 32:15)."

"Of obedience ranked above offering: to obey is better than sacrifice, and to hearken than the fat of rams (1Sa 15:22)."
